canonical_statement: For arbitrary topological spaces X and Y, a subset E of X, and a globally continuous map f : X -> Y, if E is connected in the nonempty convention then the direct set image f(E) is connected in that same convention.

statement_selection.catalog_claim: The continuous image of a connected set is connected.
statement_selection.selected_form: The canonical root follows the inspected Stacks Project Lemma 5.7.2 wording: global Continuous f, direct image f '' s, and nonempty IsConnected.
statement_selection.local_global_resolution: Pinned mathlib's ContinuousOn statement is strictly more general. It is recorded as an alternate that implies the global root through Continuous.continuousOn; the reverse implication is not claimed.
statement_selection.review_boundary: This resolves the intake's formal local-versus-global choice source-faithfully. Intake master acceptance, an independent review of the source/convention map, historical source identity, complete correction disposition, and H0 remain open.

domain_and_universes: universes u v; implicit alpha : Type u and beta : Type v; arbitrary TopologicalSpace instances on both; implicit s : Set alpha; total f : alpha -> beta
hypotheses: IsConnected s, definitionally s.Nonempty and IsPreconnected s
Continuous f on the full source space
conclusion: IsConnected (f '' s), using direct set image and the same nonempty convention.

alternate_encodings.status: credited sharper alternate implies canonical root; converse deliberately unclaimed

boundary_cases.empty_source: excluded because IsConnected empty is false; kernel-checked by empty_source_not_connected

boundary_cases.constant_map: included; constant_image_connected checks every connected nonempty source
boundary_cases.other_included_cases: noninjective and nonsurjective maps, empty ambient source only when an IsConnected subset can be supplied, non-Hausdorff and indiscrete spaces
boundary_cases.excluded_substitutions: IsPreconnected as the root, whole-space range forms, subtype/surjectivity forms, path connectedness, and any extra separation, injectivity, or surjectivity premise
